Confirming a competitor’s registered marks

Businesses with no US trademark interest
recommendedIndustries: Any business holding or seeking a US trademark

Authoritative federal record

name: EDGAR

operator.name: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission

publicAccess.notes: investor.gov states EDGAR "provides free public access to corporate information". The overall access posture is not established, so the level stays unknown.

bestFor: Reading a US public company’s filed disclosures at source
Due diligence on entities subject to SEC reporting
notRecommendedFor: Private companies with no SEC filing obligation
Marketing exposure
recommendedIndustries: Any US entity with an SEC reporting obligation
pros: Free public access to filings as they were filed
Primary source for United States securities disclosure
cons: Covers only entities that carry an SEC filing obligation
Locating the right disclosure requires familiarity with SEC form types
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-04 from investor.gov, an SEC-operated site, which states that EDGAR "provides free public access to corporate information". sec.gov refuses non-browser clients, so the company-search address cited here is the one investor.gov links to. Entries arise from federal filing obligations. There is no route by which a company asks to be included.

name: BrokerCheck
description: Free FINRA tool for researching the registration history, qualifications and disclosure events of US brokerage firms, investment adviser firms and the individuals registered with them.

operator.name: Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA)

publicAccess.notes: finra.org states BrokerCheck "is a free tool from FINRA".

bestFor: Checking whether an investment professional or firm is registered in the United States
Reviewing disclosure events before engaging a broker or adviser
notRecommendedFor: Firms outside United States securities registration
Use as a general company directory
pros: Free to search with no account required
Draws on the CRD and IARD registration systems rather than self-reported profiles
cons: Limited to firms and individuals inside United States securities registration
Not a marketing listing: entries cannot be created on request
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-04 from finra.org, which states BrokerCheck "is a free tool from FINRA". Data originates in the Central Registration Depository (CRD) and the SEC’s Investment Adviser Registration Depository (IARD), populated through mandatory registration forms, so entries arise from licensing rather than submission. FINRA is a self-regulatory organisation, not a government agency, and the record is categorised finance rather than government for that reason.

name: USAspending.gov
description: Federal award transparency database operated by the Treasury Bureau of the Fiscal Service, publishing transaction-level contracts, grants, loans and direct payments reported by agencies under the DATA Act, with recipient profiles keyed by UEI.

operator.name: U.S. Department of the Treasury, Bureau of the Fiscal Service

publicAccess.notes: Search and bulk downloads are free; no account is required.

bestFor: Establishing whether an organisation has received federal money, and how much
Tracing a recipient across awards by UEI rather than by name
notRecommendedFor: Confirming that a company legally exists
Checking good standing or licensing
pros: Transaction-level detail with free bulk download and no account
Recipient profiles expose UEI, address and corporate parent openly
cons: Recipient identity resolution is weak: one company can appear under several UEIs and name spellings
Receiving federal money is not evidence of legal existence or good standing
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-04. Operated by Treasury’s Bureau of the Fiscal Service under FFATA (2006) and the DATA Act (2014); agencies report, no entity submits or pays. One company can hold several recipient profiles under different ids — "LOCKHEED MARTIN CORPORATION" has at least three — so a name search does not resolve to a single entity. This is the open route to award data: the SAM.gov contract-data surface covering the same ground requires an account, and FPDS.gov is retired.

name: SAM.gov Entity Information
description: Federal award registration record operated by GSA, holding the registrations organisations must complete to bid for federal contracts or receive federal assistance, including the Unique Entity ID and the Responsibility/Qualification records formerly published as FAPIIS.

operator.name: U.S. General Services Administration, Integrated Award Environment

publicAccess.notes: Public entity data is free to search. GSA states that sensitive and for-official-use-only entity data requires federal CAC or PIV sign-in, so part of the record is not public.

bestFor: Checking whether an organisation is registered to receive federal awards
Resolving a Unique Entity ID before searching award data
notRecommendedFor: Confirming incorporation, which happens at state level
Establishing ownership, share capital or financial position
pros: The controlling record for federal award eligibility, including the UEI
Absorbs the former FAPIIS responsibility and qualification records in one place
cons: Entity data is self-reported and revalidated only at annual renewal, so it goes stale
Socio-economic self-certifications here are not SBA-adjudicated certifications
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-04. GSA states FAPIIS records "have moved to SAM.gov" and are now called Responsibility/Qualification records within entity information, so no separate FAPIIS record is published. Registration and UEI assignment are free and SBA warns businesses away from paid intermediaries. Not an incorporation register: US companies are formed at state level. The DUNS-to-UEI transition completed in April 2022, and older award data may still show both. Shares the sam.gov platform with the Exclusions register, but the two have different access models: entity registration data requires authentication and the exclusions data does not.

name: FDIC BankFind Suite
description: Authoritative record of every FDIC-insured depository institution, keyed by FDIC certificate number, covering insurance status, branch offices, structure changes and filed financial reports.

operator.name: Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation

publicAccess.notes: Free with no account; an open API serves the same data.

bestFor: Confirming that a bank is FDIC-insured and reading its certificate record
Tracing mergers, acquisitions and branch structure over time
notRecommendedFor: Credit unions, which are insured and supervised separately
Holding companies as such, which are not the unit of record here
pros: The definitive answer on deposit-insurance status, with the Summary of Deposits
Free API and bulk data alongside the search interface
cons: The interface is JavaScript-only, so the raw page carries no institution data
Absence proves only that an entity is not FDIC-insured, not that it is unregulated
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-04 from the FDIC Bank Data Guide and the BankFind Suite host. Records arise from deposit-insurance certification and supervisory reporting under the Federal Deposit Insurance Act; there is no listing application and no fee to appear. BankFind, Reports & Comparisons, Branch Office Deposits, Bank Structure Changes and Financial Reporting are five presentations of one dataset, not five registers.

name: OCC Financial Institution Search
description: Search over the national banks and federal savings associations chartered by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, covering the charter roster, Community Reinvestment Act evaluations, enforcement actions and corporate applications.

operator.name: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency

publicAccess.notes: Free with no account across all three surfaces.

bestFor: Confirming a national bank charter and reading OCC enforcement history
Checking a pending corporate application such as a merger or new charter
notRecommendedFor: State-chartered banks and credit unions
Non-bank financial firms
pros: Charter numbers, CRA evaluations and enforcement actions from the chartering regulator
The corporate applications pipeline is public, which few registers expose
cons: Fragmented across three tools on two different hosts, so one lookup rarely suffices
Covers only OCC-supervised institutions; enforcement by other agencies is elsewhere
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-04. Records arise from chartering and licensing under the National Bank Act and Home Owners’ Loan Act, from statutory CRA examination, and from OCC enforcement authority. The Financial Institution Lists (the authoritative charter roster) and Corporate Applications Search are alternative front ends to the same OCC record sets.

name: Investment Adviser Public Disclosure
description: SEC disclosure system for investment advisers, publishing Form ADV filings by SEC- and state-registered adviser firms, their representatives, and Exempt Reporting Advisers including private fund managers.

operator.name: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission

publicAccess.notes: Free with no account; Form ADV documents and bulk files download without charge.

bestFor: Reading an adviser’s Form ADV brochure for fees, conflicts and assets under management
Checking Exempt Reporting Advisers, including private fund and venture managers
notRecommendedFor: Broker-dealers, whose record is BrokerCheck
Corporate securities filings such as 10-K or S-1, which are in EDGAR
pros: Form ADV Parts 2 and 3 brochures are published in full, which BrokerCheck does not present
Covers Exempt Reporting Advisers that appear in no broker-dealer register
cons: Shares one CRD/IARD index with FINRA BrokerCheck, so much of the record overlaps it
The SEC states it has not approved the filed information and cannot guarantee its accuracy
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-04. Records arise from registration and Form ADV reporting under the Investment Advisers Act of 1940. adviserinfo.sec.gov and BrokerCheck return identical records in identical order over a shared field schema: they are two branded surfaces over one FINRA-operated index. It is a distinct register on shared infrastructure rather than an independent dataset: the legal basis, the Form ADV documents and the Exempt Reporting Adviser population are genuinely different. The underlying IARD filing system is operated by FINRA on the SEC’s behalf.

name: FinCEN MSB Registrant Search
description: List of businesses that have filed a Registration of Money Services Business with FinCEN under the Bank Secrecy Act, covering money transmitters, cheque cashers, currency dealers and comparable providers.

operator.name: Financial Crimes Enforcement Network, U.S. Department of the Treasury

publicAccess.notes: Free with no account.

bestFor: Checking whether a money services business has filed its federal BSA registration
notRecommendedFor: Treating registration as evidence that a business is legitimate or supervised
State money transmitter licensing, which is a separate regime
pros: Free, immediate confirmation that a federal BSA registration was filed
The only public federal list of money services business registrants
cons: Entries are entirely self-declared and are not vetted by FinCEN before publication
FinCEN itself warns that registration is not an endorsement and must not be relied on as one
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-04. Appearance results from a mandatory filing of FinCEN Form 107 under 31 CFR 1022.380; there is no fee and no way to buy a listing. FinCEN publishes a fraud warning on the search page stating that a business should not be trusted merely because it appears here. Federal registration is separate from state money transmitter licensing, and a firm present in one but not the other is itself a due-diligence signal.

name: NFA BASIC
description: Background Affiliation Status Information Center published by the National Futures Association, showing CFTC registration status, NFA membership and regulatory actions for derivatives firms, commodity pool operators, trading advisers and associated individuals.

operator.name: National Futures Association

publicAccess.notes: Free with no account.

bestFor: Checking CFTC registration and NFA membership for a futures or derivatives firm
Reading regulatory and arbitration actions against a commodity trading adviser or pool operator
notRecommendedFor: Securities broker-dealers and investment advisers, which have their own registers
pros: Single lookup for CFTC registration status, NFA membership and disciplinary history
Mandatory membership means the population is comprehensive for regulated derivatives firms
cons: The operator is a private self-regulatory body, not a federal agency
Scope is derivatives only; dual registrants must also be checked in securities registers
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-04. NFA is not a federal agency: it is a registered futures association designated by the CFTC, with mandatory membership, to which the Commission has delegated registration processing. Included in the federal layer because the registration it evidences is federal, but a reader must not mistake the operator for a government body.

name: NPPES NPI Registry
description: Public enumeration of every assigned National Provider Identifier, covering individual practitioners and organisational healthcare providers, with taxonomy codes and practice addresses as supplied by the provider.

operator.name: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, U.S. Department of Health and Human Services

publicAccess.notes: Free to search and to download in bulk; no account required.

bestFor: Resolving a healthcare provider or organisation to its National Provider Identifier
Confirming the taxonomy and practice address a provider has reported
notRecommendedFor: Verifying a professional licence, which CMS expressly disclaims
Establishing Medicare enrolment or billing approval
pros: Complete, free and downloadable enumeration of US healthcare providers
The join key that connects most other federal healthcare datasets
cons: CMS states that holding an NPI does not establish that a provider is licensed or credentialed
Provider-supplied details go stale; deactivation is not always prompt
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-04. Records arise from statutory identifier assignment under the HIPAA Administrative Simplification NPI standard; enumeration is free. CMS disclaims licensure, so an NPI is an identifier rather than a licence: the register assigns and publishes an identifier, it does not license anyone. Forcing it into the licence type would misdescribe what an NPI proves.

name: FDA Establishment Registration and Device Listing
description: Registry of medical device establishments registered with the FDA Center for Devices and Radiological Health, together with the devices each has listed, searchable by establishment, owner or operator, product code or proprietary name.

operator.name: U.S. Food and Drug Administration, Center for Devices and Radiological Health

publicAccess.notes: Search results and bulk download files are free.

bestFor: Confirming that a medical device manufacturer or importer is registered with the FDA
Finding which devices an establishment has listed
notRecommendedFor: Reading registration as FDA approval or clearance, which the FDA expressly denies
pros: Establishment and device listing in one searchable federal register
Free bulk files alongside the interface
cons: Results are capped at 100 establishments per search, so common names cannot be enumerated
Registration is not FDA approval or clearance of the establishment or its products
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-04. Records arise from mandatory registration and listing under the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act. An annual establishment registration user fee is payable to the FDA, but that is a regulatory fee for registration itself, not payment for a listing, and there is no route by which a firm asks to be listed. The 100-result cap is stated by the FDA on the search page. Shares the accessdata.fda.gov application host with the CDER drug establishment register; the two are separate FDA systems covering different regulated populations, recorded as separate systems despite the shared hostname.

name: Tax Exempt Organization Search
description: IRS search over five tax-exemption datasets, covering organisations eligible to receive deductible contributions, automatic revocations, filed Form 990 series returns, Form 990-N filings and determination letters.

operator.name: Internal Revenue Service, Tax Exempt and Government Entities Division

publicAccess.notes: Free with no account; the host applies bot mitigation to automated clients but presents no user-facing challenge.

bestFor: Confirming federal tax-exempt status and whether contributions are deductible
Reading a nonprofit’s filed Form 990 series returns
notRecommendedFor: State charity registration or solicitation licensing, which is entirely absent
Real-time status checks, given the staggered dataset refresh
pros: Five IRS datasets, including automatic revocations, in one free search
Determination letters and Form 990 returns are published directly
cons: Datasets are posted on staggered dates, so a status check can be weeks out of date
Federal exemption says nothing about state-level registration to solicit donations
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-04 from the IRS TEOS FAQ. Records arise from statutory exemption recognition and mandatory annual information-return filing. The IRS charges a user fee for a determination letter application, but that is a statutory application fee rather than a directory listing fee. Dataset posting dates observed on the FAQ ranged across early June 2026, which is why data currency is called out in the cons.

name: Patent Public Search
description: USPTO search over granted US patents and published applications, providing full document text and images for the public patent record.

operator.name: United States Patent and Trademark Office, U.S. Department of Commerce

publicAccess.notes: Free with no account; certified copies are a separate paid USPTO service.

bestFor: Searching the full text of granted US patents and published applications
Establishing that a patent was issued and reading the document as granted
notRecommendedFor: Determining current patent ownership, which is frozen at grant here
Checking whether a patent is still in force
pros: Full-text and image access to the US patent corpus at no charge
The public replacement for the retired legacy USPTO search tools
cons: Assignee data is frozen at publication or grant, so it is not a current ownership record
Maintenance-fee status, expiry and post-grant proceedings are not shown
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-04. Records arise from patent examination and grant under 35 U.S.C.; filing and issue fees are prosecution fees, not listing fees. Deliberately distinguished from USPTO Patent Center, which is NOT published: USPTO states that from 11 September 2025 identity verification is required and guest users can no longer access it, so it is not a public resource. Current patent ownership is recorded in the separate Assignment Search system, which this register does not cover.

name: DMCA Designated Agent Directory
description: Copyright Office directory of agents designated by online service providers to receive copyright infringement notifications, resolving a platform to a legal entity name and a service-of-process address.

operator.name: U.S. Copyright Office, Library of Congress

publicAccess.notes: Free to search with no account.

bestFor: Resolving a consumer-facing platform brand to its legal entity and contact address
Finding where to send a copyright notice for a US online service
notRecommendedFor: Treating a designation as proof that safe harbour applies
pros: Often the quickest route from a brand name to a legal entity and address
Free and directly searchable
cons: The Copyright Office does not verify submissions, so entries can be stale or inaccurate
Records begin with the December 2016 electronic system; earlier paper designations are absent
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-04. Records arise from the statutory designation requirement in 17 U.S.C. § 512 and 37 C.F.R. § 201.38 — a provider files because safe-harbour eligibility is conditioned on it. The Office charges a filing fee. It does not publish the amount on the directory pages. The Office performs no vetting: presence evidences a designation, not that safe harbour actually applies.

name: TTB List of Permittees
description: Published lists of holders of federal alcohol basic permits, released by the Alcohol and Tobacco Tax and Trade Bureau as frequently requested FOIA records covering producers, wholesalers and importers.

operator.name: Alcohol and Tobacco Tax and Trade Bureau, U.S. Department of the Treasury

publicAccess.notes: Files download freely with no account or challenge.

bestFor: Confirming that a business holds a federal alcohol basic permit
Enumerating permitted importers or wholesalers in bulk
notRecommendedFor: Looking up a single business quickly, since there is no search interface
State alcohol licensing, which is separate
pros: Bulk downloadable permit lists published as a standing FOIA release
Served without the bot challenge that blocks the TTB label-approval search
cons: There is no search interface at all; the entire system is a set of downloadable files
Tax records are withheld by statute, so the lists carry no financial detail
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-04. Records arise from federal licensing under the Federal Alcohol Administration Act, and publication is a FOIA obligation TTB describes in its own words. A non-technical user cannot look up one business: the importer list alone runs to roughly 21,000 rows. TTB notes that Internal Revenue Code section 6103 protects taxpayer records, which is why no financial data appears.

name: Permitted Customs Brokers Listing
description: Customs and Border Protection list of customs brokers holding a federal permit to transact customs business, published by port with company contact details.

operator.name: U.S. Customs and Border Protection, Office of Trade, U.S. Department of Homeland Security

publicAccess.notes: Free to read with no account.

bestFor: Confirming that a customs broker holds a CBP permit before engaging one
notRecommendedFor: Freight forwarding and NVOCC services, which are licensed by a different agency
Any check needing licence dates, status history or disciplinary record
pros: Direct confirmation that a broker is permitted, from the permitting agency
Organised by port, which matches how importers actually choose a broker
cons: Seven columns and no licence number, issue date, expiry or status history
Lists permitted broker entities, not individually licensed broker employees
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-04 by reading the published table. Records arise from federal licensing and permitting under 19 CFR part 111; brokers pay statutory application and permit fees, and nothing is paid to appear. This is the thinnest approved record set in the wave, which the transparency and moderation factors reflect: presence or absence is all it establishes.

name: Federal Maritime Commission Ocean Transportation Intermediary List
description: Federal Maritime Commission lists of licensed ocean freight forwarders and non-vessel-operating common carriers that have met the Commission’s licensing, financial responsibility and tariff requirements.

operator.name: Federal Maritime Commission, Bureau of Certification and Licensing

publicAccess.notes: Free to search with no account.

bestFor: Confirming that a freight forwarder or NVOCC is compliant with FMC requirements
notRecommendedFor: Customs brokerage, which is permitted by a different agency
Any history of sanctions or complaints, which the list does not carry
pros: Confirms licensing plus proof of financial responsibility and tariff publication together
Distinguishes freight forwarders from NVOCCs, which are different licences
cons: The list reflects current compliance, not licence status, so a licensed NVOCC with a lapsed tariff filing simply disappears
Current state only: no history, sanctions or complaint record
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-04. Entries arise from FMC licensing and registration under the Shipping Act, conditioned on statutory proof of financial responsibility and tariff publication. The distinction between compliance and status is an easily missed trap: absence from the list does not by itself prove that a company is unlicensed.

name: FCC Universal Licensing System
description: Federal Communications Commission register of wireless radio licences and the applications behind them, keyed by call sign and FCC Registration Number, covering licensee name, radio service, status and expiry.

operator.name: Federal Communications Commission, Wireless Telecommunications Bureau

publicAccess.notes: Free to search with no account.

bestFor: Confirming that a company holds an FCC wireless licence and reading its status and expiry
Tracing licence applications and ownership disclosures for spectrum holders
notRecommendedFor: Broadcast, cable, satellite or equipment authorisation, which use separate FCC systems
pros: Authoritative licence status, expiry and licensee identity direct from the regulator
Ownership disclosure filings are searchable alongside the licences
cons: Search sessions are server-scoped, so results cannot be linked or cited by URL
Covers Wireless Bureau licensing only; other FCC estates live in separate systems

A licence record establishes that a licence exists in the Wireless Bureau’s system. It does not establish that the licensee is transmitting, that the licence is unrestricted, or that the holder is an authorised telecommunications carrier — carrier registration sits in a separate FCC system.

Absence does not establish that a transmission is unlawful or unauthorised. This system covers Wireless Bureau licensing only, and broadcast, cable, satellite and equipment authorisations are held in separate FCC systems.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-04. Records arise from FCC licensing and spectrum authorisation under the Communications Act. License Search, Advanced and Specialized Search, Application Search, License Archive Search and Ownership Disclosure Search are modes of one platform, one registry. The session-scoped search produces no stable deep links, so a result cannot be cited or re-checked by URL.

name: FCC Form 499 Filer Database
description: Registration records for providers required to file the Telecommunications Reporting Worksheet, giving the 499 Filer ID, the carrier’s legal name, its holding company and its designated agent for service of process.

operator.name: Federal Communications Commission, Consumer and Governmental Affairs Bureau

publicAccess.notes: The search form is public and free, but the results endpoint sits behind bot management that refuses automated clients; a browser is needed to retrieve results.

bestFor: Confirming that a telecoms or VoIP provider has registered with the FCC
Finding a carrier’s holding company and agent for service of process
notRecommendedFor: Financial analysis: the revenue data behind the worksheet is not published
pros: One of the few federal registers that publishes a holding company and an agent for service of process
Mandatory annual filing keeps the registrant population current
cons: The results endpoint is protected by bot management and needs a real browser
Reported revenue data is not disclosed, so it establishes registration only

A filer entry establishes registration for the Telecommunications Reporting Worksheet. It does not establish that the carrier holds any licence, that it is currently providing service, or that it is financially sound.
Absence does not establish that a provider is unauthorised. This database records worksheet filers, and licensing and authorisation records are held in separate FCC systems.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-04. Entries arise from a mandatory filing: the FCC states that providers are required to register using Form 499-A and update at least annually. Data collection is performed by the Universal Service Administrative Company on the FCC’s behalf. The interactive results endpoint sits behind an Akamai challenge that refuses non-browser clients, which is a real access limitation even though the register itself is free.

name: FAA Aircraft Registry
description: The US civil aircraft register, published by the FAA Civil Aviation Registry, giving registration status, registered owner, manufacturer, model and airworthiness classification for each N-numbered aircraft.

operator.name: Federal Aviation Administration, Civil Aviation Registry

publicAccess.notes: Search is free; complete aircraft records must be ordered separately through the FAA records request service.

bestFor: Confirming the registered owner of a specific US-registered aircraft
Establishing aircraft registration status from the N-number
notRecommendedFor: Judging airworthiness, which the FAA expressly warns against
Enumerating a corporate fleet, since aircraft are often held by separate entities
Settling title or legal ownership — registration records the registered owner, not clear title
pros: Free lookup of the registered owner of any US civil aircraft, by N-number or serial
Long-standing and stable, with a deep historical record
cons: Owner-name search is literal, so fleets held through subsidiaries are effectively invisible
Complete records are a separate paid request; the free search returns a summary
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-04. Aircraft registration is a federal statutory requirement under 49 U.S.C. chapter 441. The literal-match limitation is concrete: a search for a well-known operator’s name returned nothing because its aircraft are registered to a differently named holding entity. This is an asset and title record rather than a corporate register, and it should be read as evidence about an aircraft, not about a company.

name: MSHA Mine Data Retrieval System
description: Mine Safety and Health Administration register of every coal and metal or non-metal mine under its jurisdiction since 1970, keyed by Mine ID and linking each mine to its operator and controlling entity alongside inspection and enforcement records.

operator.name: Mine Safety and Health Administration, U.S. Department of Labor

publicAccess.notes: Free with no account; bulk data files are published openly.

bestFor: Linking a mine to its operator and controlling entity
Reading inspection and enforcement history for a mining operation
notRecommendedFor: Mineral title, permits or royalties, which are outside MSHA jurisdiction
Beneficial ownership: the controller chain records legal control, not natural persons
pros: The controller-to-operator-to-mine chain is the closest thing in the federal layer to a corporate control map
Complete back to 1970 with open bulk data
cons: The interactive system is an embedded business-intelligence report rather than a web application
Jurisdiction is safety and health only, so it says nothing about a company’s wider standing
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-04. Mine IDs, operator and controller records and enforcement records arise from mandatory registration, inspection and reporting under the Federal Mine Safety and Health Act. The controller chain must be described as legal control, not beneficial ownership: there is no publicly searchable US federal beneficial-ownership register, and this must not be presented as a substitute for one.

name: FSIS Meat, Poultry and Egg Product Inspection Directory
description: Directory of establishments holding a USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service grant of inspection, listing establishment number, activities carried out and the establishment’s commercial identifier.

operator.name: Food Safety and Inspection Service, U.S. Department of Agriculture

publicAccess.notes: Free to view and download; further detail requires a FOIA request rather than payment.

bestFor: Confirming that a meat, poultry or egg establishment holds a federal grant of inspection
Identifying what activities an establishment is approved to carry out
notRecommendedFor: Enforcement history and recalls, which FSIS publishes separately
State-inspected establishments, which are outside federal jurisdiction
pros: Authoritative confirmation of federal inspection status with the establishment number
Publishes a commercial identifier, which makes supply-chain matching practical
cons: The interactive surface is a data visualisation rather than a record-by-record search
Carries no enforcement, recall or inspection-finding detail
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-04. Inclusion follows a federal grant of inspection under the Federal Meat Inspection Act, Poultry Products Inspection Act and Egg Products Inspection Act. Serious use means downloading the published file rather than using the embedded visualisation, though the data itself is strong.

name: SAM.gov Exclusions
description: Governmentwide record of parties excluded from federal contracts, subcontracts and federal assistance, listing firms and individuals debarred, suspended, proposed for debarment, declared ineligible or voluntarily excluded by any federal agency.

operator.name: U.S. General Services Administration, Integrated Award Environment

publicAccess.notes: Exclusion records are returned to unauthenticated requests, unlike entity registrations on the same platform.

bestFor: Checking whether a firm or individual is currently barred from federal contracts or assistance
Identifying which agency imposed an exclusion and on what ground
notRecommendedFor: Reading absence as proof of eligibility, compliance or good character
Health care programme exclusions, which HHS OIG maintains separately
pros: The single governmentwide view of federal exclusions, free and without an account
Records carry the excluding agency, exclusion type and effective dates
cons: Matching is by name with no identity adjudication, so false positives are routine and the burden falls on the searcher
Many records carry no UEI or CAGE code, which makes reliable machine matching impossible
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-04. Records are created by federal suspension and debarment officials under FAR Part 9 and 2 CFR Part 180; no entity submits itself and no fee exists. It is a separate register from SAM.gov Entity Information rather than a tab of it: entity registration data requires authentication and the exclusions data does not, and the two rest on different legal authority with different subject populations. Absence from this list means only that no federal agency has recorded an exclusion; it establishes nothing about eligibility or conduct.

name: HHS OIG List of Excluded Individuals and Entities
description: List of individuals and organisations currently excluded from Medicare, Medicaid and all other federally funded health care programmes, maintained by the HHS Office of Inspector General under the Social Security Act.

operator.name: Office of Inspector General, U.S. Department of Health and Human Services

publicAccess.notes: Both the online search and the complete downloadable file are free.

bestFor: Screening a provider or supplier before engaging or paying them under a federal health programme
Reading the statutory ground and effective date of an exclusion
notRecommendedFor: Checking whether a party was EVER excluded, since reinstated parties are removed entirely
Federal procurement debarment, which is recorded in SAM.gov Exclusions
pros: Complete current exclusion list, downloadable in full at no cost
Carries the statutory authority, exclusion date and any reinstatement or waiver detail
cons: Current exclusions only: reinstated parties are deleted from the file, so past exclusions cannot be checked here
OIG warns that a database hit is not proof of identity and requires separate confirmation before it is relied on
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-04 from oig.hhs.gov. Records arise from exclusion actions imposed by HHS OIG under sections 1128 and 1156 of the Social Security Act; no party submits or pays.
